questions.question: A man is undergoing treatment for T cell leukemia.

parts.text: What is a viral infection associated with this leukemia?
Name another clinical syndrome associated with this virus.
Name three routes of transmission.

questions.model_answer:
a) Viral infection associated with T-cell leukemia: Human T-lymphotropic virus type 1 (HTLV-1), associated with adult T-cell leukemia/lymphoma (ATLL).
b) Another clinical syndrome: HTLV-1-associated myelopathy/tropical spastic paraparesis (HAM/TSP).
c) 3 routes of transmission: (1) mother-to-child, predominantly via breastfeeding; (2) sexual contact; (3) parenteral - blood transfusion or shared needles (injection drug use).

parts.text: Name 6 different viruses and an associated malignancy with each one

questions.model_answer: (1) Human papillomavirus - cervical/anogenital/oropharyngeal squamous cell carcinoma (2) Hepatitis B virus - hepatocellular carcinoma (3) Hepatitis C virus - hepatocellular carcinoma (4) Epstein-Barr virus - Burkitt lymphoma, Hodgkin lymphoma, nasopharyngeal carcinoma, or PTLD (5) HHV-8 (KSHV) - Kaposi sarcoma (6) HTLV-1 - adult T-cell leukemia/lymphoma.

questions.question: PM 26. Woman from the Caribbean with T cell lymphoma

parts.text: What virus can cause this? (1)
What are three primary modes of transmission? (1.5)
What is one clinical finding of this virus? (1)

cohort_answer.text: HTLV-1. Transmission: bloodborne, sexual, breast milk. Clinical finding: Tropical spastic paraparesis (TSP) - progressive insidious onset weakness, hyperreflexia, clonus of lower limbs (may be asymmetrical), paresthesias, lumbar pain, urinary symptoms common.

questions.question: Q31 (2015). Woman from the Caribbean with T cell lymphoma.

parts.text: A) Viral association?
B) 3 modes of acquisition/transmission?
C) Other complications of the virus?

cohort_answer.text: A) HTLV-1. B) Vertical transmission (mother to child, primarily breastmilk); Sexual transmission; Parenteral (IVDU or transfusions). C) Neuro: HTLV-associated myelopathy/tropical spastic paraparesis, ALS, peripheral neuropathy. Skin: infective dermatitis, crusted scabies, eczema, seborrheic dermatitis. Eyes: uveitis, keratoconjunctivitis sicca. Rheum: polymyositis. Cancer: Adult T cell leukemia-lymphoma.

questions.question: You see a pregnant woman presenting with evidence of human T-lymphotropic virus.

parts.text: List TWO non-infectious diseases associated with this virus.
List TWO organisms or infectious conditions that are more common with this virus.
List the ONE most important strategy to avoid transmission.

questions.model_answer:
a) 2 non-infectious diseases associated with HTLV-1: (1) adult T-cell leukemia/lymphoma (ATLL); (2) HTLV-1-associated myelopathy/tropical spastic paraparesis (HAM/TSP).
b) 2 infectious conditions more common with HTLV-1: (1) Strongyloides stercoralis hyperinfection/disseminated strongyloidiasis; (2) increased susceptibility to tuberculosis (crusted/Norwegian scabies is also an accepted answer).
c) Most important strategy to avoid transmission (in this pregnant patient): avoid breastfeeding (formula feed the infant), as breast milk is the predominant route of mother-to-child transmission.

questions.question: A 45 year old Caribbean woman is undergoing treatment for T-cell lymphoma.

parts.text: What is one infectious etiology of her condition?
What are the THREE routes of transmission of this agent?
Name ONE other condition associated with this agent.

questions.model_answer:
a) Infectious etiology: Human T-lymphotropic virus type 1 (HTLV-1).
b) 3 routes of transmission: (1) mother-to-child, predominantly via breastfeeding; (2) sexual contact; (3) parenteral - blood transfusion/shared needles.
c) Another associated condition: HTLV-1-associated myelopathy/tropical spastic paraparesis (HAM/TSP) (Strongyloides hyperinfection also acceptable).

parts.text: A) Name 2 places in the world where it is endemic (besides the Caribbean)
What are 3 modes of acquisition?

cohort_answer.text: A) HTLV-1 endemic to central Africa, Caribbean basin, parts of South America, southwestern Japan; HTLV-2 endemic to South America and central Africa. Modes: Vertical transmission (mother to child via breastfeeding); Sexual; Injection drug use, SOT, transfusions.

questions.question: A pregnant woman is diagnosed with HTLV-1.

parts.text: Name two non-infectious conditions/diseases associated with HTLV-1
Name two infectious diseases/syndromes associated with HTLV-1
What one thing do you suggest to her to prevent vertical transmission

cohort_answer.text: Non-infectious: Adult T cell leukemia lymphoma (ATLL); HTLV-I-associated myelopathy (HAM), also known as tropical spastic paraparesis (TSP). Infectious: Strongyloides hyperinfection syndrome; TB; Leprosy; Infective dermatitis; Schistosoma mansoni. Prevention of vertical transmission: Avoid breastfeeding; screening of blood donors; safe sex; avoid sharing needles

parts.text: List 4 viruses associated with bloodborne transmission (not HIV or hepatitis)

cohort_answer.text: HTLV-1, Zika, CMV, EBV, West Nile, Ebola

parts.text: Name 6 different viruses that cause cancer and what type of cancer?

questions.model_answer: (1) Human papillomavirus (HPV) - cervical, anal, vulvar/vaginal/penile, and oropharyngeal squamous cell carcinoma. (2) Hepatitis B virus - hepatocellular carcinoma. (3) Hepatitis C virus - hepatocellular carcinoma. (4) Epstein-Barr virus - Burkitt lymphoma, nasopharyngeal carcinoma, Hodgkin lymphoma. (5) Human herpesvirus-8 (HHV-8/KSHV) - Kaposi sarcoma, primary effusion lymphoma, multicentric Castleman disease. (6) Human T-lymphotropic virus type 1 (HTLV-1) - adult T-cell leukemia/lymphoma (Merkel cell polyomavirus causing Merkel cell carcinoma is another acceptable answer).
questions.cites: Mandell pp. 1917-1920 (HPV); other viruses beyond this chapter
